doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First soprano saxophone at five and first public performance
summary: His father imported a soprano saxophone in 1953, taught him, and nine months later presented him at a school show with a swing piece among three tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: How old were you the first time you picked up an instrument and tried to play?

In 1953 my father imported a soprano [saxophone] from the factory in Paris; probably imported it before because he had to order it. And he taught me how to play it, and nine months later he presented me in public. So, I was five years old when I first picked up an instrument, maybe a little less than that.
Nine months after picking up an instrument he presented you in public. How did he present you in public, and where did he present you?

Now, the end of a semester in a school that I used to go to in my neighborhood—the name of the school is Emila Ascada—and every year, they have like a little music and dance school there, more dance, you know and acting. And most of them were girls, and some of them played piano and recited poems. So, my father presented me with a saxophone quintet.
Was it safe to say that what you were playing was classical music?

Not really. We’ll have to come back to this later, because my throat is going. There was a combination; I played like maybe three pieces. There was a swing piece because my father liked swing music very much. I don’t remember, it was “Who’s Sorry Now”, the other one “Alavera port Tu,” and I don’t remember the third one.
